0|3fe2895cfecd03ac74977f32102b966b6589f481|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"mm: fix page leak with multiple threads mapping the same page
We have an application with a lot of threads that use a shared mmap backed
by tmpfs mounted with -o huge=within_size.  This application started
leaking loads of huge pages when we upgraded to a recent kernel.
Using the page ref tracepoints and a BPF program written by Tejun Heo we
were able to determine that these pages would have multiple refcounts from
the page fault path
column2: but when it came to unmap time we wouldn't drop the

column1: number of refs we had added from the faults.
I wrote a reproducer that mmap'ed a file backed by tmpfs with -o
huge=always
column2: and then spawned 20 threads all looping faulting random

column1: offsets in this map
column2: while using madvise(MADV_DONTNEED) randomly for huge

column1: page aligned ranges.  This very quickly reproduced the problem.
The problem here is that we check for the case that we have multiple
threads faulting in a range that was previously unmapped.  One thread maps
the PMD
column2: the other thread loses the race and then returns 0.  However at

column1: this point we already have the page
column2: and we are no longer putting this

column1: page into the processes address space
column2: and so we leak the page.  We

column1: actually did the correct thing prior to f9ce0be71d1f
like Kirill copied what we do in the anonymous page case.  In the
anonymous page case we don't yet have a page
column2: so we don't have to drop a

column1: reference on anything.  Previously we did the correct thing for file based
faults by returning VM_FAULT_NOPAGE so we correctly drop the reference on
the page we faulted in.
Fix this by returning VM_FAULT_NOPAGE in the pmd_devmap_trans_unstable()
case
column2: this makes us drop the ref on the page properly

column1: reproducer no longer leaks the huge pages.
